frameworks.name: Buyback Evaluation Framework

takeaways: Only purchase equities if you can comfortably endure 50% or greater declines and plan to hold for a decade or more.
Use low‑fee index funds as the backbone of a portfolio; active managers rarely outperform after fees.
Evaluate buyback proposals by asking whether the company retains enough cash for growth and whether the repurchase price is below intrinsic value.
Avoid making buying or selling decisions based on short‑term price movements or external opinions.
Recognize that large, diversified businesses like Berkshire can sustain modest underperformance versus the S&P 500 while still delivering long‑term value.

frameworks.name: Six Rich Dad Lessons
frameworks.summary: A concise set of principles—money works for you, think like an investor, manage risk, treat home as a liability, prioritize cash flow, and develop financial education—that guide parents in raising financially empowered children.

takeaways: Teach children to ask "how can I afford it?" instead of saying "I can't afford it" to activate problem‑solving.
Encourage discussions about money and business at the dinner table to normalize financial literacy.
View your home as a potential liability; prioritize cash‑flow‑positive assets over equity‑only holdings.
Shift from working for money to making money work for you through investments and entrepreneurship.
Replace entitlement mindsets with self‑reliance by modeling budgeting, saving, and creating income streams.

frameworks.name: Carnegie Secret
frameworks.summary: A two‑part principle of personal achievement that, when recognized and applied, drives wealth and success across any field, emphasizing mental readiness, decisive action, and consistent application.

takeaways: Recognize that a single, universal principle—the Carnegie secret—underlies the success of the world’s most prosperous individuals and can be identified when you are mentally prepared.
Make decisions swiftly once you have all the facts; hesitation signals a lack of the decisive mindset needed to execute the secret effectively.
Study the patterns of proven achievers rather than copying surface tactics, extracting the underlying principle that drives their results.
Apply the secret consistently across business, personal, and leadership contexts; its effectiveness is not limited to any specific industry.
Prioritize mindset and readiness over formal education, understanding that the secret relies on internal conviction rather than external credentials.
